In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Brinkmann graph''' is a 4-[[regular graph]] with 21 vertices and 42 edges discovered by Gunnar Brinkmann in 1992.<ref>Brinkmann, G. "Generating Cubic Graphs Faster Than Isomorphism Checking." Preprint 92-047 SFB 343. Bielefeld, Germany: University of Bielefeld, 1992.</ref> It was first published by Brinkmann and Meringer in 1997.<ref name="BM97">Brinkmann, G. and Meringer, M. "The Smallest 4-Regular 4-Chromatic Graphs with Girth 5." Graph Theory Notes of New York 32, 40-41, 1997.</ref>

It has [[chromatic number]] 4, [[chromatic index]] 5, radius 3, diameter 3 and girth 5. It is also a 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected graph]] and a 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected graph]]. It is the smallest 4-regular graph of girth 5 with chromatic number 4.<ref name="BM97"/> It has [[book thickness]] 3 and [[queue number]] 2.<ref>Jessica Wolz, ''Engineering Linear Layouts with SAT''. Master Thesis, University of Tübingen, 2018</ref>
The graph is not [[1-planar_graph|1-planar]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Pupyrev | first = Sergey
 | editor-first1 = Vida | editor-last1 = Dujmović | editor-first2 = Fabrizio | editor-last2 = Montecchiani
 | contribution = OOPS: Optimized One-Planarity Solver via SAT
 | title = Proc. 33rd International Symposium on Graph Drawing and Network Visualization (GD 2025)
 | series = Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics (LIPIcs)
 | year = 2025 | volume = 357 | pages = 14:1–14:19
 | doi = 10.4230/LIPIcs.GD.2025.14
 | isbn = 978-3-95977-403-1 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

By [[Brooks’ theorem]], every ''k''-regular graph (except for odd cycles and cliques) has chromatic number at most ''k''. It was also known since 1959 that, for every ''k'' and ''l'' there exist ''k''-chromatic graphs with girth ''l''.<ref>{{citation
 | doi = 10.4153/CJM-1959-003-9
 | last = Erdős | first = Paul | author-link = Paul Erdős
 | journal = Canadian Journal of Mathematics
 | pages = 34–38
 | title = Graph theory and probability
 | volume = 11
 | year = 1959| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> In connection with these two results and several examples including the [[Chvátal graph]], Branko Grünbaum conjectured in 1970 that for every ''k'' and ''l'' there exist ''k''-chromatic ''k''-regular graphs with girth ''l''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Grünbaum | first = B. | author-link = Branko Grünbaum
 | doi = 10.2307/2316101
 | issue = 10
 | journal = American Mathematical Monthly
 | pages = 1088–1092
 | title = A problem in graph coloring
 | volume = 77
 | year = 1970
 | publisher = Mathematical Association of America
 | jstor = 2316101}}.</ref> The Chvátal graph solves the case ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''l''&nbsp;=&nbsp;4 of this conjecture and the Brinkmann graph solves the case ''k''&nbsp;= &nbsp;4, ''l''&nbsp;=&nbsp;5. Grünbaum's conjecture was disproved for sufficiently large ''k'' by Johannsen, who showed that the chromatic number of a [[triangle-free graph]] is O(Δ/log&nbsp;Δ) where Δ is the maximum vertex degree and the O introduces [[big O notation]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Reed | first = B. A. | authorlink = Bruce Reed (mathematician)
 | doi = 10.1002/(SICI)1097-0118(199804)27:4<177::AID-JGT1>3.0.CO;2-K
 | issue = 4
 | journal = Journal of Graph Theory
 | pages = 177–212
 | title = ω, Δ, and χ
 | volume = 27
 | year = 1998}}.</ref> However, despite this disproof, it remains of interest to find examples and only very few are known.

The [[chromatic polynomial]] of the Brinkmann graph is ''x''<sup>21</sup> − 42''x''<sup>20</sup> + 861''x''<sup>19</sup> − 11480''x''<sup>18</sup> + 111881''x''<sup>17</sup> − 848708''x''<sup>16</sup> + 5207711''x''<sup>15</sup> − 26500254''x''<sup>14</sup> + 113675219''x''<sup>13</sup> − 415278052''x''<sup>12</sup> + 1299042255''x''<sup>11</sup> − 3483798283''x''<sup>10</sup> + 7987607279''x''<sup>9</sup> − 15547364853''x''<sup>8</sup> + 25384350310''x''<sup>7</sup> − 34133692383''x''<sup>6</sup> + 36783818141''x''<sup>5</sup> − 30480167403''x''<sup>4</sup> + 18168142566''x''<sup>3</sup> − 6896700738''x''<sup>2</sup> + 1242405972''x'' {{OEIS|A159192}}.

==Algebraic properties==
The Brinkmann graph is not a [[vertex-transitive graph]] and its full automorphism group is isomorphic to the [[dihedral group]] of order 14, the group of symmetries of a [[heptagon]], including both rotations and reflections.

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of the Brinkmann graph is <math>(x-4)(x-2)(x+2)(x^3-x^2-2x+1)^2</math><math>(x^6+3x^5-8x^4-21x^3+27x^2+38x-41)^2</math>.
